Answer: To Ehren Bragg, When I was in my 50s, I got an earlier shingles vaccine, which was OK, but the SHINGRIX vaccine is far more effective, so I also got the newer SHINGRIX vaccine when it came out. I got the SHINGRIX vaccine at my local Costco, and I am glad I did! You are smart to get it at 50 now that you’re officially old enough to get the vaccine. I’ve known people who caught shingles in their 20s, but that’s rare. I also have a friend who caught it at age 80 and was in PAIN for months. Because I had chickenpox as a child (long before the chickenpox vaccine was a reality), this vaccine will prevent me from getting the dreaded shingles rash, or at least it will prevent me from getting a really bad infection.[1] NOTE: The shingles vaccine does NOT prevent you from getting chickenpox. If you never had chickenpox as a child, you should get the chickenpox vaccine, not the shingles vaccine. I do not think you would need the shingles vaccine if you had never had chickenpox.[2] [3] (Note: It is spelled “SHINGRIX,” not “Chingrix,” because it echoes the name “shingles,” a viral infection that makes its presence known by a painful rash. You are open to getting shingles if you have ever had chickenpox, because both are caused by the varicella-zoster virus.) SIDE EFFECTS: As others have said, when you get the SHINGRIX vaccine, you might have a sore arm for a few hours, and you might be a little tired for a day, but it certainly is far less painful than getting shingles. I have friends and family who have suffered from shingles, and they were in agony for weeks. —Sarah Madden, #8211, Written and ©Copyrighted ♥ 29 March 2024 QUESTION: Has anyone had the Chingrix vaccine? Question: How can you delete a deleted comment so that no trace of the comment is left?
Answer: To William Shaw, Merely deleting a comment may remove it from an answer, but it will still show up in your edit log, unless you take an additional step. I have discovered a simple way to eliminate any history of a comment I wrote and then deleted. We own our comments, so we should be able to control how they are viewed. NOTE: If you merely delete a comment, its text will still reside in your edits log, albeit with a reddish background to indicate it was deleted. NOT FOR REPRODUCTION OR FOR TRANSLATION. WRITTEN and copyrighted by Sarah Madden. If you posted a comment you later want to delete, and you also want to erase any trace of it from your edit logs, go into the comment, select the entire thing, replace it with a period (or an innocuous word), SAVE the edited comment, then delete the comment. Done. Because you have deleted the comment, your edit logs will only display how the comment looked the last time it was saved. In my case, the deleted *comment* is merely a period. This is particularly useful if you are being slammed by a troll, but you want to erase any connection to the troll. It also means your edit log provides nothing *interesting* regarding your comments, should anyone want to take a screenshot. I use this technique whenever I delete my comments, even the ones that are not controversial. The screenshot below shows the edit history of a comment I deleted. Notice there is NOTHING BUT A PERIOD in the edit log showing the comment was deleted.
